deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages). Sigma = {Delta_i}, i in I, card Sigma = n, is a finite system of pseudo-lines in a projective plane X. X~ is the double cover (sphere) and D~ is the double cover (a circle) of a pseudo-line D. Grothendieck studies the set of all auxiliary pseudo-lines D placed relative to Sigma, up to isotopy, ordered by specialization. A specialization makes D pass through more vertices of the arrangement, or collapse a 'triangle of specialization' T, or even make D coincide with some Delta_{i0} (the 'super-critical' case on the next page). In oriented-matroid language this is the poset of single-element extensions of the rank-3 oriented matroid of Sigma: the extension space.

Top lines (end of the previous discussion). A specialization D -> D' induces an injection Gen_1(D) -> Gen_1(D') between the sets of codimension-one generizations, i.e. the edges incident at each point. The complement of the image has exactly two elements. Locally the stratification looks like an arrangement of 'pivot curves': each vertex s on D gives two half-edges, pivoting D around s in the two directions.

Main construction: the 'canonical cellular embedding' Str(Sigma) of the specialization graph Gamma(Sigma) into a surface. Str(Sigma) is the stratified structure on the space of pseudo-lines relative to Sigma, the analogue of the dual projective plane, whose 2-cells are generic positions of D. Edges of Gamma are oriented by specialization, and vertices D are classified by the pattern of incident arrows, as the drawings show:
- stable: all edges leave D;
- semi-stable: exactly two edges arrive;
- critical: at least four arrive;
- critical extremal: all edges arrive (four thick incoming arrows in the drawing).
The vocabulary is borrowed from GIT.

Weights. Each edge of Gamma carries a weight in N*: the number of edges of D (in the arrangement Sigma' = Sigma together with D) swallowed by the specialization. The orange/green figure shows two such cases: D sweeping a triangle T, and D moving through a multiple point.

Local (rotation) structure at a vertex D. The cyclic order of the edges at D is read off the circle D~. The 'angular sectors' (corners) between consecutive edges correspond to arcs of D~ between two consecutive specialization or cospecialization points. Each corner is weighted by the number of edges of Sigma' on the corresponding arc.

Outcome. The data form a combinatorial map (carte cellulaire) on a surface, with an oriented graph and with weighted edges and weighted corners.

Identity: at every vertex D, the sum of the weights of all edges at D plus the sum of the weights of all corners at D equals 2n. Reason: generically D~ meets the 2n lifted points of the Delta_i and so is cut into 2n segments. Every segment is either collapsed by one of the specializations or lies on one of the arcs.

Open point. A question, partly illegible, asks to describe the admissible weightings, i.e. which weighted maps arise.

Next page. The weights are used to blow up the polygon Pol(D) into a 2n-gon with antipodal symmetry, in canonical bijection with the oriented lines I~.

Purpose: a combinatorial-topological description of the 'dual' of a pseudo-line arrangement (the space of all pseudo-lines relative to it) as a weighted map on a surface. This is in the spirit of Grothendieck's contemporaneous 'cartes' of the Esquisse.
errors: The edge orientation convention is not made explicit on this page. Since a pivot edge has both endpoints more special than its interior, 'arriving/leaving' cannot mean plain specialization in the naive dual-plane picture; the orientation must come from another rule, probably the direction in which a triangle of specialization is collapsed. The classification is therefore stated before its basis is fixed.

The surface into which Gamma(Sigma) is embedded is not identified on this page; one expects the projective plane, or a sphere after passing to orientations. Neither manifoldness nor the topological type is argued.

The 2n identity is a counting statement that is correct only if each segment of D~ is counted exactly once, either in an edge weight or in a corner weight. Multiple points (where the swallowed count depends on multiplicity) are only sketched, so the identity is plausible but unchecked in degenerate cases.

ideas.what: Space of all pseudo-lines relative to a pseudo-line arrangement, stratified by specialization, viewed as a 2-dimensional cell complex: a 'dual plane' Str(Sigma).
ideas.modern_name: Extension space (poset of single-element extensions) of a rank-3 oriented matroid; dual of a topological projective plane
ideas.usually_credited_to: Single-element extensions: Las Vergnas (1978). Extension spaces: Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993). Extension of arrangements to topological planes: Goodman–Pollack–Wenger–Zamfirescu (1994).

ideas.what: Canonical cellular embedding of the specialization graph Gamma(Sigma) into a surface, with local rotation read off the double cover D~.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial map / ribbon graph structure on the extension space (cellular structure of the dual pseudo-plane)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; implicit in work on extension spaces and topological planes.
ideas.where_published: Conceptually adjacent to the 'cartes' of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this construction is not there.

ideas.what: Classification of vertices into stable, semi-stable, critical and critical-extremal by incoming versus outgoing specialization edges.
ideas.modern_name: Local types of strata; GIT-flavoured terminology. Closest notion: 'simple' versus 'non-simple' cocircuits / vertices of the extension.

ideas.what: Weighted map: edge weights equal the number of D-edges swallowed by a specialization; corner weights equal the number of D-edges on the arc of D~. Local identity: the total weight at each vertex is 2n.
ideas.modern_name: Local degree/count identity for the cut circle D~ (2n intersection points of a great pseudo-circle with n pseudo-circles)

ideas.what: Gen_1(D) -> Gen_1(D') is injective with a two-element complement under specialization.
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of the face poset of the extension space (each additional incident vertex adds two pivot half-edges)

missed.claim: In 1983–84 Grothendieck treats the space of pseudo-lines compatible with an arrangement (the rank-3 extension space) as a canonical cellular surface carrying an oriented, weighted combinatorial map. This anticipates the extension-space programme of Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) and the topological-plane dual of Goodman–Pollack et al. (1994), and links it to his own theory of cartes from the Esquisse period.
missed.quote: Plongement cellulaire canonique Str(Σ) ... de Γ(Σ) dans une surface ... on trouve une carte cellulaire à graphe orienté, et à arêtes et "coins" pondérés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Viewing rank-3 extension spaces as dessins/maps with local weight conditions is not a standard viewpoint in oriented-matroid theory. It could give a combinatorial handle on the dual pseudo-plane and on the extension space conjecture.

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses, but does not answer, the problem of characterizing which weighted oriented maps, satisfying the local 2n condition at each vertex, arise as Str(Sigma) of some pseudo-line arrangement. This would be a duality or reconstruction theorem.
missed.quote: Qu. : décrire ... poids, pour lequel ... D) ... Somme des pondérations ... est égale à 2n (si n = card Σ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Such a characterization would be a new combinatorial description of rank-3 oriented matroids via their extension spaces. To my knowledge no such result is in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up an apparently unpublished and unstudied construction: the extension space of a pseudo-line arrangement as a canonical weighted cellular map on a surface, with a local 2n identity and a GIT-style vertex typology. It predates the oriented-matroid literature on extension spaces. The individual statements are elementary, though, and the construction is only sketched with an open question, so it is a notable unpublished detail rather than a surprising theorem.

'The [?] structure cellulaire locale' should read 'La structure cellulaire locale'.
'correspond à une arc' should read 'correspond à un arc'.
'est égal au son poids des arêtes angulaires' likely reads 'est égal au poids des secteurs angulaires'.
'une {+cartes [?] cellulaires+}' should read 'une carte cellulaire'; '{+à graphes orientés+}' should read 'à graphe orienté'.
'et à arêtes et "arcs" pondérés' should read 'et à arêtes et "coins" pondérés' (corners).
